questions.question: What should you do if you are in a serious car crash?
questions.explanation: Stop your vehicle and move it off the road if possible. If anyone is hurt, call 911 and help them. You must report the crash to police if there is an injury, a death, or more than $1,000 in property damage.

questions.question: Your brake lights tell other drivers that you are:
questions.explanation: Brake lights tell other drivers that you are slowing down or stopping. Your brake lights must always work when you drive.

questions.question: The best safety protection in a crash is:

options.text: Only a lap and shoulder belt.
Both a lap/shoulder belt and an airbag.

questions.correctAnswerText: Both a lap/shoulder belt and an airbag.
questions.explanation: Safety belts double your chance of surviving a crash. Airbags used with safety belts provide extra protection in a front-end crash. Wear both your shoulder and lap belts.

questions.question: If you are in an accident, what should you do?
questions.explanation: Stop your vehicle right away. Move it out of traffic if you can. Call the police and ask for an ambulance if needed. Do not move injured people, but stop heavy bleeding with direct pressure. Wait for emergency vehicles.

questions.question: If you are getting tired while driving, you should:

options.text: Stop and rest or let someone else drive.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop and rest or let someone else drive.
questions.explanation: Take breaks every hour on long trips to avoid tired driving. Share driving with another person so you can both rest.

questions.question: A solid yellow arrow on a traffic signal means:

options.text: Speed up to make the turn before the light changes.
You do not need to signal your turn.
Be ready to stop and let oncoming traffic go first.

questions.correctAnswerText: Be ready to stop and let oncoming traffic go first.
questions.explanation: A solid yellow arrow means the green arrow is ending. Get ready to stop and let oncoming traffic pass before you turn.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: A school or school crosswalk is near.
Slow down, drive carefully, and watch for children.

questions.explanation: This sign is placed near schools to warn drivers to slow down, drive carefully, and watch for children.

questions.question: You see the driver ahead using one hand and talking to a passenger. You should:

options.text: Stay farther away from that vehicle.
Know that driver is not paying full attention and is less safe.
Do not drive the same way.

questions.explanation: Do not get distracted by passengers, looking for things in your car, reading, or daydreaming while driving. If another driver seems distracted, stay back because they are more likely to crash.

questions.question: If you drive faster and pass cars often on a two-lane road, you will:

options.text: Get to your destination faster and safer.
Increase your chance of a crash.

questions.correctAnswerText: Increase your chance of a crash.
questions.explanation: Avoid passing other cars on two-lane roads. Every time you pass, your risk of a crash increases.

questions.question: When should you not pass another vehicle?

options.text: When a school bus has flashing red lights.

questions.explanation: Never pass if there is a car coming, if a curve or hill blocks your view, at an intersection, before or on a railroad crossing or bridge, or in any no passing zone. Do not pass a stopped school bus with flashing red lights unless you are on the opposite side of a divided road.

questions.question: Like alcohol and drugs, drowsiness can:
questions.explanation: Not getting enough sleep causes poor driving. Drowsiness slows your reaction time, reduces awareness, and weakens your judgment — just like drugs and alcohol.

questions.question: You see pedestrians near the road. You should:

options.text: Speed up to leave the area quickly.

questions.explanation: Watch for pedestrians who may cross your path. If you see pedestrians near the road, slow down and be ready to stop if needed.

questions.question: You reach a railroad crossing with lowered gates and flashing lights. You should:

options.text: Drive around the gates if you don't see a train.
Stop behind the gates, wait for the tracks to clear, then go when the gates lift.
Slow down and drive around the gates.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop behind the gates, wait for the tracks to clear, then go when the gates lift.
questions.explanation: You must stop at a railroad crossing when signs, warning devices, or flaggers warn you of a train. It is illegal to drive around lowered gates.

questions.question: Always signal when:

options.text: Pulling into or out of a parking space.
Pulling into traffic from an alley or parking area.

questions.explanation: Always use your turn signal when changing lanes, pulling into or out of a parking space, or pulling into traffic from an alley or parking area. Tell other drivers what you're doing to prevent accidents.

questions.question: A reflective orange triangle on the back of a vehicle means:
questions.explanation: A reflective orange triangle on the back means the vehicle travels slower than 25 mph. You may see this on farm equipment, construction vehicles, and horse-drawn wagons.

questions.question: You are on the interstate and pass your exit. You should:

options.text: Quickly cut across traffic to make your turn.
Make a U-turn to go back to the exit.
Continue driving and use the next exit.
Put your vehicle in reverse to go back to the exit.

questions.correctAnswerText: Continue driving and use the next exit.
questions.explanation: Don't make a sudden turn to catch your exit. If you miss it, go to the next exit.

questions.question: You missed your exit on the freeway. You should:

options.text: Make a U-turn through the median.
Pull onto the shoulder and back up to the exit.
Flag down a police officer to escort you back.

questions.explanation: Take the next exit if you miss yours. Do not stop, back up, swerve across lanes, or turn around on the highway. These actions are illegal and dangerous.

questions.question: After drinking several beers, the only way to reduce alcohol's effects is:
questions.explanation: Only time removes alcohol from your body. Coffee, exercise, or cold showers will not speed this up. It takes about one hour to process one drink.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: No traffic is allowed in this lane.
You must merge into this lane.

questions.explanation: A steady green arrow pointing down over a lane means you may use that lane.

questions.question: The best way to avoid hydroplaning is to:

options.text: Keep your tires in good condition.
Slow down on wet or slushy roads.
Watch for standing water or puddles.

questions.explanation: On wet roads, cars take longer to stop and may skid on sharp turns. Don't use cruise control in wet or icy conditions. Reduce speed and drive carefully.

questions.question: What is the only proven way to remove alcohol or drugs from your body?
questions.explanation: Alcohol enters your body quickly but leaves slowly. Cold showers, coffee, and exercise do not lower your blood alcohol level. Time is the only way to reduce it.

questions.question: Pedestrians in crosswalks and at intersections always have the right-of-way.
questions.explanation: Pedestrians have the right-of-way when crossing at an intersection. A crosswalk exists at any place where two streets meet, whether it is marked or not.

questions.question: A pedestrian starts crossing after the "Don't Walk" signal flashes. They are in the middle of the street when your light turns green. You should:

options.text: Go if you have the right-of-way.
Go if the pedestrian is not in your lane.
Wait until the pedestrian finishes crossing.

questions.correctAnswerText: Wait until the pedestrian finishes crossing.
questions.explanation: At a green light, you must let any vehicle, bicycle, or pedestrian in the intersection cross first. If a pedestrian is in the intersection, wait until they are completely across before you go.

questions.question: At a stop sign without a crosswalk, you must stop before entering the intersection.
questions.explanation: At a stop sign, make a complete stop at the stop line if one exists. If there is no stop line, stop before the crosswalk. If there is no crosswalk, stop before entering the intersection.

questions.question: Before changing lanes or passing another vehicle, you should:

options.text: Check your mirrors and blind spots.

questions.explanation: Signal other drivers before moving left or right. Always check your mirrors and look over your shoulder to check your blind spot before moving your vehicle.
